method: The listed basmati rice quantity is the dry, uncooked weight. Follow the cooking and assembly steps below for this measured portion.

Start the 70g dry basmati rice first: this is the uncooked weight. Use the water quantity and cooking time on the rice packet; simmer until tender, then drain if the packet method requires it. Keep covered briefly while finishing the pan, then serve immediately.
Wash and drain the 100g spinach. Check the 150g salmon fillet for bones. Keep it as a fillet for pan cooking, then flake it after cooking.

Warm a non-stick frying pan over a medium-low heat; this recipe does not include frying oil. Put in the salmon fillet, skin-side down if it has skin. Cook for 4–5 minutes, turn carefully and cook for another 3–5 minutes until the centre is opaque, steaming hot and flakes easily; a thicker piece needs longer. Transfer to a clean plate; keep the pan for the vegetables. Never reuse the plate or utensils that held the raw food without washing them.

Put the 120g chopped tomatoes and 25g medium curry paste into the same frying pan. Stir over a medium-low heat, then cover and simmer gently for 5 minutes. Stir twice; keep the heat low enough that the tomato liquid does not boil dry.
Add the washed spinach in two handfuls, cover for 1 minute, then stir. Cook for another 2–3 minutes until wilted throughout.

Flake the cooked salmon into large pieces and fold into the pan at the end; avoid breaking it up with vigorous stirring. Heat everything together over a low heat for 2–3 minutes, stirring gently, until steaming hot throughout. Spoon over the freshly cooked rice and serve immediately.

review.notes: Large opaque cooked salmon flakes with wilted spinach and tomato curry, white long-grain basmati; no fresh garnish.
